mechanism: Scopolamine's anticholinergic effects may be potentiated by prednisone's immunosuppressive and CNS effects, while prednisone may increase intraocular pressure which scopolamine can also elevate.
action: Monitor for anticholinergic adverse effects (dry mouth, urinary retention, confusion) and intraocular pressure; use lowest effective doses and consider alternative antiemetics if prolonged use anticipated.
